- If sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate; reduce forecast slightly.
- If sentiment is negative (≤0.33) or neutral (0.00), model often underestimates; increase forecast to align with mean reversion or volatility.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >10% from prior peak), model frequently overshoots and fails to correct; cap forecast at 1–2% below peak or adjust downward after 3–5 days.
- Model shows strong mean reversion bias: if 30d forecast is flat or trending upward, true outcome often reverses downward; apply downward bias if sentiment turns negative.
- When sentiment history shows alternating highs/lows (e.g., 1.00, 0.33, 1.00), model tends to lag; adjust forecast 1–2 days ahead to match sentiment momentum.
- If true outcome exceeds 30d forecast by >5% and sentiment is positive, model is under-reacting; increase forecast by 1–3% to capture sentiment-driven momentum.
- If forecast is flat or rising slowly but true outcome spikes, model misses volatility; add 1–2% upward bias if sentiment is bullish and price is below 70.00.
